This involves intentionally selling investments that have declined in value to "realize" those losses. These realized capital losses can then be used to offset any capital gains you've incurred from other investments, dollar-for-dollar. If your total capital losses exceed your total capital gains, you can further use up to \$3,000 of those remaining losses to offset your ordinary income each year, such as your salary. This applies across all your taxable accounts, so careful coordination is key. Other specialized trusts, like Special Needs Trusts or Charitable Trusts, serve unique purposes but also come with specific limitations on asset use or beneficiary control, balancing specific goals against general flexibility.

Please know that navigating these choices is a journey many people undertake, and your proactive approach is commendable. While these explanations offer a starting point, the nuances of your specific financial situation, family dynamics, and long-term goals are paramount.
